domain_symbols.open_problems: world-famous unsolved problems and partial results
domain_symbols.symbolic: symbolic expressions used by this domain

rules.name: Riemann Hypothesis statement
rules.output_form: all nontrivial zeros of zeta(s) lie on Re(s) = 1/2
rules.operation: State the conjecture controlling the distribution of prime numbers via the explicit formula.
examples: First 10^13 nontrivial zeros lie on the critical line (numerical evidence)
counterexamples: A single off-line zero would refute the hypothesis
common_errors: Confusing trivial zeros at negative even integers with nontrivial zeros

rules.name: P vs NP statement
rules.operation: Ask whether every NP problem is solvable in polynomial time.
examples: SAT, TSP-decision, integer programming are NP-complete
counterexamples: Most experts conjecture P != NP, but no proof is known
common_errors: Treating NP-hard as the same as NP-complete

rules.name: Navier-Stokes existence and smoothness
rules.input_form: incompressible 3D Navier-Stokes with smooth divergence-free initial data
preconditions: Periodic or whole-space domain, finite-energy initial data
rules.operation: Ask whether smooth solutions of 3D incompressible Navier-Stokes always remain smooth.
examples: Leray weak solutions exist globally but uniqueness/smoothness unknown
counterexamples: 2D Navier-Stokes is fully resolved (global smooth solutions exist)
common_errors: Conflating Euler (inviscid) blow-up scenarios with viscous case

rules.name: Yang-Mills mass gap
rules.output_form: quantum Yang-Mills theory on R^4 exists with a positive mass gap
rules.operation: Construct a mathematically rigorous quantum Yang-Mills theory and prove a strictly positive mass gap.
examples: Lattice simulations strongly support a mass gap for SU(3) Yang-Mills
counterexamples: Free abelian Maxwell theory has no mass gap
common_errors: Assuming perturbative QCD already constitutes a rigorous construction

rules.name: Hodge conjecture
rules.input_form: smooth projective variety X over C
rules.output_form: every Hodge class on X is a rational linear combination of classes of algebraic cycles
rules.operation: Identify which rational cohomology classes are algebraic.
counterexamples: The generalized Hodge conjecture has known counterexamples without rationality
common_errors: Confusing Hodge classes with Chern classes

rules.name: Birch and Swinnerton-Dyer conjecture
rules.input_form: elliptic curve E over Q with L-function L(E,s)
rules.output_form: rank(E(Q)) = order of vanishing of L(E,s) at s = 1
preconditions: E a non-singular elliptic curve over Q
rules.operation: Connect arithmetic rank of Mordell-Weil group to analytic order of L-function vanishing.
examples: Proven for analytic rank 0 and 1 (Gross-Zagier, Kolyvagin)
counterexamples: The full conjecture for rank >= 2 remains open
common_errors: Conflating algebraic rank with torsion subgroup size

rules.name: Poincare conjecture (resolved)
rules.operation: Cite the only solved Millennium problem to date, proven via Ricci flow with surgery.
examples: Perelman declined the Fields Medal and the prize
common_errors: Confusing topological and smooth versions in higher dimensions

rules.name: Twin prime conjecture
rules.output_form: there are infinitely many such pairs (open)
rules.operation: State the unsolved infinitude of twin primes.
examples: Zhang (2013) proved bounded gaps < 70,000,000; Maynard tightened to <= 246
common_errors: Confusing twin primes with Sophie Germain primes

rules.name: Goldbach's conjecture
rules.output_form: n = p + q for some primes p, q (open in general)
examples: Ternary Goldbach proven by Helfgott (2013) for all odd n >= 7
common_errors: Confusing binary and ternary Goldbach statements

rules.name: Collatz conjecture
rules.input_form: n positive integer; iterate n -> n/2 if even, 3n+1 if odd
examples: Tao (2019): almost all orbits reach values arbitrarily small
common_errors: Treating heuristic random-walk arguments as proofs

rules.name: abc conjecture
rules.input_form: coprime a + b = c in Z>0, radical rad(abc)
rules.output_form: for every eps > 0, c <= K(eps) rad(abc)^{1+eps} for finitely many exceptions
rules.operation: Bound the size of c by the product of distinct primes dividing abc.
examples: Implies Fermat's Last Theorem asymptotically and many Diophantine results
counterexamples: Mochizuki's IUT proof remains controversial in the broader community
common_errors: Treating the conjecture as universally accepted as proven

rules.name: Beal conjecture
rules.input_form: A^x + B^y = C^z with x,y,z >= 3 and positive integers A,B,C
rules.output_form: A, B, C share a common prime factor (open)
rules.operation: Generalize Fermat's Last Theorem to mixed exponents.
examples: Equivalent to a special case implied by modularity-type results
counterexamples: No counterexample known; large computer searches confirm

rules.name: Hadamard maximal determinant problem
rules.output_form: max |det(M)| <= n^{n/2}, equality requires n = 1, 2, or 4k
rules.operation: State the Hadamard matrix existence conjecture as the equality condition.
examples: Smallest open order historically was 668 (now closed); current open orders pushed higher
counterexamples: For non-multiple-of-4, equality is unattainable beyond 1, 2
common_errors: Confusing Hadamard matrices with Hadamard transforms

rules.name: Unique games conjecture
rules.input_form: unique label cover instance with parameter eta
rules.output_form: deciding (1-eta vs eta) satisfiability is NP-hard for all eta > 0
rules.operation: State the UGC underlying many optimal inapproximability results.
examples: Implies optimal hardness for MAX-CUT (Khot et al.)
counterexamples: The related 2-to-2 games conjecture has been proven; UGC itself remains open
common_errors: Treating the 2-to-2 result as resolving UGC

rules.name: Smooth 4D Poincare conjecture
rules.input_form: closed smooth 4-manifold M homotopy equivalent to S^4
rules.output_form: M diffeomorphic to S^4 (open in smooth category)
rules.operation: State the still-open smooth 4-dimensional Poincare problem.
counterexamples: R^4 has uncountably many exotic smooth structures
common_errors: Conflating topological and smooth categories in dimension 4

rules.name: Hilbert's 16th problem (part 2)
rules.input_form: planar polynomial vector field of degree n
rules.output_form: uniform bound H(n) on number of limit cycles (open)
rules.operation: Ask for a finite uniform bound on limit cycles by degree.
examples: Existence of finitely many limit cycles for each individual field is known
counterexamples: No bound is known even for n = 2
common_errors: Confusing existence of finitely many cycles per field with a uniform bound
